experiment: Phase 4a predictor gate G2 — RE-RUN with live GRIFFIN (post slice-1 finalize fix)
operating_point: mini dense container (H=256, L=4, I=512), HOT_FRAC=0.5, GRIFFIN=1, Q36_PROFILE_TOK_K=64, disjoint corpora A/B (~250 tokens each + 64 new), greedy
decision: FAIL — predictor +0.0000 vs both baselines (rule: >= +0.05); runtime work NOT unlocked
diagnosis: coverage saturates at 1.0 for EVERY selector on synthetic weights: per-neuron energy mass concentrates in a few norm-dominant rows, so any top-K that includes them covers ~all energy. This supersedes 4a's original 'sets are constant' diagnosis: sets DO vary per token (window sim: jaccard(t,t-1)=0.17, 99% differ from token 0), but the coverage metric is insensitive on synthetic data. The discriminator only bites on real weights, where energy mass spreads over content-dependent sets.
consequence: predictor stays offline-only; the Phase 5 real-weights arm is unchanged and is the only place G2 can pass. Window cache value is likewise a Phase-5/battery question, not a synthetic one.
